crop.name: Winter squash / pumpkin, Cucurbita (the dark, pale-striped, slightly flattened round fruit reads as a kabocha-type Cucurbita maxima; a summer-squash-type Cucurbita pepo cannot be fully excluded)
crop.distinguishing_features: Very large, broadly triangular to heart-shaped leaves with shallow lobes, coarsely toothed margins, a pale palmate main-vein network radiating from the petiole, and a bristly-hairy surface with scattered whitish flecks; thick, angular, deeply grooved, hairy petioles and vines that all converge on one crown; coiling branched tendrils at the nodes; a large dark green fruit with pale longitudinal stripes and fine light speckling resting on the mulch, plus a smaller immature striped fruit still carrying its shrivelled brown flower at the tip; growth is a single deliberate hill spreading over the bed rather than scattered individuals.

weeds.name: Grasses (volunteer cereal / annual grasses germinating from the straw mulch; blade width varies, so more than one grass species is likely)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Narrow strap-shaped blades with strictly parallel veins and no petiole, no branching veins, smooth or faintly ridged surfaces, sharply pointed tips, and blades that emerge in tufts directly from the mulch and sheath the stem; colour is a flatter blue-green than the squash, and they never bear tendrils, teeth, or a lobed outline.

weeds.name: Purslane-type succulent broadleaf seedling (Portulaca oleracea, probable)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Small rosettes of thick, glossy, spoon-shaped leaves in opposite/whorled clusters on smooth fleshy stems lying close to the soil; leaves are hairless and untoothed with a rounded tip and no visible vein network, quite unlike the hairy, veiny, toothed squash foliage.

weeds.name: Round-leaved creeping broadleaf (mallow / ground-ivy type, Malva neglecta or similar)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Small kidney-shaped to circular leaves with scalloped (crenate) margins and palmate veins, borne singly on slender wiry petioles rising from a low creeping seedling; shares palmate venation with the squash but is a fraction of its size, has rounded scallops instead of sharp teeth, and no tendrils or bristly stems.

weeds.name: Small trifoliate legume (clover / medic seedling)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Three small oval leaflets joined at one point on a thin stalk, smooth and darker green, hugging the mulch surface — a compound leaf, whereas every squash leaf is a single large simple blade.

non_plant_material: Dry straw / chopped cereal-stem mulch covering most of the bed surface
Bare dry cracked soil visible between the mulch
Small grey-white down feather lying on the mulch
Dried, shrivelled brown flower remnant attached to the immature fruit
Dead curled brown leaf litter and broken dry stem fragments
scene.hard_to_tell_apart: The main risk is at the crop's own edges: young, pale, silver-flecked squash leaves seen edge-on or in low light look like a separate rough-leaved broadleaf weed, and the toothed, grey-green leaf lobes shaded under the canopy could be mistaken for a thistle or dock rosette — following the blade back to a thick grooved hairy petiole on the shared crown identifies them as squash. Conversely, grass blades constantly cross over and lie against the squash stems and fruit, so a region containing a stem may hold both. Squash tendrils are thin and green enough to be confused with fine grass leaves or weed stems. The tiny broadleaf seedlings in the open mulch are at a stage where purslane, mallow and clover are only separable by leaf thickness, margin and leaflet count, and any of them could equally be an unrelated seedling.
